first-french-empire.t: Napoleon Bonaparte's empire, which held much of continental Europe until its defeat in 1814 and, after the Hundred Days, again at Waterloo in 1815.
first-french-empire.o: In 1799 Napoleon Bonaparte took part in a coup against the Constitution of the Year III, became First Consul, and was proclaimed Consul for life on 2 August 1802. The Senate gave him the title Emperor of the French on 18 May 1804, and he was crowned on 2 December 1804, ending the [[s:french-first-republic|French First Republic]].
first-french-empire.r: The state was still formally called the French Republic until October 1808. Napoleon kept many social gains of the Revolution while suppressing political liberty, and the Napoleonic Code increased legal equality and legalised divorce. The Concordat of 1801 confirmed the Catholic Church as the majority church. At its height in 1812 the empire had 130 departments and a population over 44 million, and Napoleon placed relatives on the thrones of satellite states such as Naples, Holland and Westphalia.
first-french-empire.e: Napoleon's 1812 invasion of Russia led to the near complete loss of his army. Paris capitulated on 30 March 1814, and he abdicated at Fontainebleau on 11 April. He returned for the Hundred Days in 1815, was defeated at Waterloo and exiled to Saint Helena, where he died in 1821. The [[s:bourbon-restoration|Bourbon Restoration]] followed.
